title: Regression firebreak for cohorted config & model rollouts with auto-repair
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight "firebreak" layer that monitors canary and A/B cohort quality metrics and invokes an automated repair workflow when a statistically significant regression is detected. The goal is to minimize blast radius for config and model changes while enabling fast, reversible rollouts with an automatic remediation path before human intervention is required.
background: We currently rely on manual inspection and coarse alerting for rollout regressions which increases time-to-mitigation and customer exposure. Previous initiatives added eval gates and cohort samplers but lack an automated remediation path that attempts safe, narrow repairs (e.g., config delta rollback, model-variant swap) before a full rollback. This ticket implements the operational layer that ties eval signals to automated actions with conservative safety heuristics.
proposed_solution: 1) Cohort definition: support deterministic user hashing cohorts and traffic-sampled canaries. 2) Metrics: compute a composite 'quality delta' across pre-registered eval sets (semantic-match, hallucination-rate, latency-p99, token-cost) and normalize by baseline variance. 3) Detection: run a sequential test (SPRT) with minimum sample floor and FDR controls to avoid noisy triggers. 4) Firebreak actions: a prioritized auto-repair pipeline with steps: a) attempt config-delta revert for changed keys (non-disruptive), b) if config revert unavailable, swap to a compatible model-variant (quantized vs fp16) or previous model version, c) if neither applies, throttle cohort and escalate. 5) Observability: store decision traces and feature-level delta for postmortem and audit. 6) Safety: conservative cool-down windows, per-customer opt-out, and manual approval gates for destructive actions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit/integ tests + simulation against replayed traffic (1 week). Phase 1: enable in shadow mode for 1% of canary traffic and verify no auto-actions (collect signal fidelity). Phase 2: enable auto-repair for internal customers (dogfood) at 0.5% cohorts for 2 weeks. Phase 3: expand to external canaries with 1% cohorts and monitor for 4 weeks. Phase 4: default on with adjustable sensitivity and SLO-backed guardrails. Each phase includes a rollback-to-plan checkpoint and a post-phase readiness review.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alerts: 1) 'firebreak-trigger' when SPRT crosses threshold; 2) 'auto-repair-failed' when the pipeline cannot restore acceptable quality in X minutes; 3) 'escalation-needed' when >Y% of active cohorts are affected. Dashboards: per-cohort quality delta, per-action success rate, time-to-repair distribution, top contributing eval metrics. Telemetry: store raw eval snapshots for 30 days for debugging. Integration: emit audit events to the Console's rollouts timeline and to the audit log (for Private deployments).
acceptance_criteria: - Firebreak can be enabled per-route and per-model; - Detection algorithm reaches target false positive rate <2% on historical traces; - Auto-repair pipeline executes one of the defined actions end-to-end in staging; - Decision traces are visible in Console with links to eval snapshots; - Rollout to dogfood cohort completes with no customer-facing incidents and documented runbook for manual override.
open_risks: - Risk of noisy metrics causing unnecessary repairs; mitigation: conservative thresholds, SPRT with minimum sample size. - Risk of incorrect config revert causing semantic mismatch; mitigation: dry-run revert in shadow and quick rollback. - Interaction with Dedicated and Private deployments where model artifacts may not be writable; mitigation: support model-variant swap only when artifact access present and fall back to throttling. - Complexity increases operational load; mitigation: start with small surface (text-generation routes) and add telemetry to measure ROI.
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Regression+Firebreak+Design (internal). PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/firebreak/pull/12. Eval set canonicalization work is tracked in PM-728. Meet: sync Tuesdays 11:00AM PT.
